purpose: Runs a batch of jobs through a fixed number of worker goroutines, collects results in job order and supports cancellation and fail-fast.

representativeFlow.name: run a job batch
representativeFlow.why: Single business action; shows channel creation, producer, workers, collector and cancellation in one function.

steps.role: builds the pool with the Upper handler and prints results
derives a cancelable context, creates channels, starts feed, workers and the closer goroutine, collects results
producer goroutine, sends jobs and closes the input channel
consumes jobs, sends results, exits on closed input or cancellation
calls the handler, wraps errors, recovers panics, records trace events
example handler, rejects empty payloads with ErrEmptyPayload

expectedFacts.statement: The input channel in is created in Pool.Run and closed by the feed goroutine (defer close(in)); the sender owns and closes it, workers only receive from it.

The output channel out is created in Pool.Run and closed by a small goroutine in Pool.Run that waits on the WaitGroup; no single worker closes it because several workers send on it. Pool.Run ranges over out until it is closed.
Pool.Run derives ctx with context.WithCancel(parent) and defers cancel(); cancelling the parent or calling cancel (fail-fast) closes ctx.Done().
Cancellation reaches feed (select on ctx.Done), workers (ctx.Err check after receiving a job and select on ctx.Done when sending a result) and the handler (receives ctx as an argument).
With FailFast set, the collector in Pool.Run calls cancel() on the first result carrying an error, which stops the remaining jobs; Run still returns parent.Err(), which is nil in that case.
A worker goroutine exits when the input channel is closed and drained, when it sees ctx cancelled, or when a result send loses the select to ctx.Done; defer wg.Done() runs on every exit path.

The feed goroutine ends when all jobs are sent (then it closes in) or when it observes ctx.Done(); Pool.Run's deferred cancel() guarantees it does observe it, so feed cannot block forever on an abandoned in channel.
Pool.Run does not return until out is closed, which happens only after every worker has finished, so workers do not outlive Run.

Deliberate leak risk: in Pool.RunWithTimeout the done channel is unbuffered. When the timeout wins the select and the function returns, the goroutine started there blocks forever on done <- res; one goroutine leaks per timed-out call. A buffered channel of capacity 1 would let it finish.
Pool.process wraps handler errors with fmt.Errorf("job %d: %w", ...), so the message gains a "job N: " prefix while errors.Is(err, ErrEmptyPayload) still works because %w keeps the chain.

Defers in Pool.process run last-in-first-out: the recover closure runs first, then the deferred trace "end"; the "begin" trace happens immediately. A handler panic is converted into a Result with a "job N: panic" error.
Workers finish in arbitrary order but Pool.Run sorts results by JobID before returning.

traps.statement: Claiming a worker closes out, or that Run closes in, is wrong.
The leak is in RunWithTimeout, not in Run; claiming Run itself leaks workers on cancellation is wrong.
Claiming the code has no goroutine leak risk is wrong.
Claiming Run returns an error when FailFast cancels is wrong; it returns parent.Err().

mustNotClaim: Run leaks worker goroutines on cancellation
